You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Comparing the source and edited images, what does the visual evidence establish about the requested move of the source mug to the right of the headphones: complete fulfillment, partial progress, no progress, or unresolved?
node.criteria: Pass only if evidence reliably establishes that the source mug itself was moved and is now to the right of the same headphones. Fail only if evidence reliably establishes that no relevant progress toward the requested move occurred. Treat as partial progress when the edited image provides credible visual evidence of an attempted or incomplete move of the source mug, even if its identity or final position is uncertain—for example, a conspicuous mug-shaped remnant or blur at its former location together with a mug on the right. Do not treat uncertainty about whether a right-side mug is the source mug as proof of no progress, and do not infer complete fulfillment from a right-side mug alone. Use unknown when the evidence cannot reliably establish either relevant progress or no progress, or cannot determine whether the requested condition is fulfilled.
node.binding: Cross-image binding: the source blue mug and the same headphones in the source and edited images. Compare the source mug with all visible edited mugs, assess their left-to-right positions relative to the headphones, and inspect the source mug’s former location for evidence of a remnant or movement, allowing for changes in scale, lighting, and appearance.

node_traces.evidence: The source shows a blue mug to the left of the headphones. In the edited image, a mug is clearly positioned to the right of the headphones, and the source mug’s former left-side location has a conspicuous blue, mug-shaped blur/remnant. Together these provide evidence that the source mug was moved toward the right; the right-side mug is beyond the headphones.

Check the node’s label mapping/routing as well: its trace says the move is only toward the right while the aggregate emits `yes` against a `partial` reference. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported."}
